concepts.title: Crops — Kharif and Rabi
concepts.description: Crops — Kharif and Rabi — part of the chapter on Food and Agriculture.
key_ideas: Core principles of crops
Step-by-step problem solving for crops
Real-world applications of crops

concepts.title: Life of a Farmer
concepts.description: Life of a Farmer — part of the chapter on Food and Agriculture.
key_ideas: Core principles of life of a farmer
Step-by-step problem solving for life of a farmer
Real-world applications of life of a farmer

concepts.title: Tools Used in Agriculture
concepts.description: Identification and usage of traditional and modern implements used by farmers to cultivate soil and harvest crops.
key_ideas: Traditional tools like the plough (hal) and sickle
Modern machinery like tractors and harvesters
Specific tools for digging and loosening soil (Khunti)

concepts.title: Steps of Farming
concepts.description: The chronological sequence of activities a farmer performs to grow a crop from a seed to a harvest ready for the market.
key_ideas: Preparing the soil (ploughing)
Sowing seeds at the right distance
Irrigation (watering) and Weeding (removing unwanted plants)
Harvesting the ripe crop

concepts.title: From Field to Market (Mandi)
concepts.description: Understanding the supply chain of how harvested crops are transported, sold at wholesale markets, and eventually reach our homes.
key_ideas: Transportation of crops via trucks or bullock carts
The role of the Mandi (Wholesale Market)
Vegetable sellers and retailers

concepts.title: Food Spoilage and Wastage
concepts.description: Recognizing signs that food has gone bad and understanding the difference between spoiling food and wasting food.
key_ideas: Signs of spoilage (smell, color change, fungus)
Conditions that speed up spoilage (heat, moisture)
The ethical importance of not wasting food

concepts.title: Methods of Food Preservation
concepts.description: Techniques used to store food for longer periods to prevent it from rotting.
key_ideas: Drying (making papads or chips)
Pickling (using salt and oil)
Freezing and canning
Boiling milk to keep it fresh

concepts.title: Sources of Water
concepts.description: Sources of Water — part of the chapter on Water.
key_ideas: Core principles of sources of water
Step-by-step problem solving for sources of water
Real-world applications of sources of water

concepts.title: Water Conservation
concepts.description: Water Conservation — part of the chapter on Water.
key_ideas: Core principles of water conservation
Step-by-step problem solving for water conservation
Real-world applications of water conservation

concepts.title: Forms of Water
concepts.description: Introduction to the three states of water: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (vapour), and how they change from one to another.
key_ideas: Water can exist as ice, liquid water, or steam
Heat turns water into vapour (evaporation)
Cooling turns vapour into water (condensation)

concepts.title: Solubility in Water
concepts.description: Exploration of how different substances interact with water, distinguishing between things that dissolve and things that do not.
key_ideas: Some solids like sugar and salt dissolve in water
Some substances like sand and chalk powder do not dissolve
Oil does not mix with water and floats on top

concepts.title: Floating and Sinking
concepts.description: Observational study of objects that float on water versus objects that sink, introducing basic concepts of buoyancy.
key_ideas: Lighter or hollow objects often float
Heavy, solid objects often sink
Shape can change whether an object sinks or floats (e.g., a ball of dough vs. a boat)

concepts.title: Safe Drinking Water
concepts.description: Understanding the difference between clean and dirty water, and methods to make water safe for consumption.
key_ideas: Not all clear water is safe to drink
Boiling kills germs in water
Filtration removes visible dirt and impurities

concepts.title: Water Pollution
concepts.description: Identifying human activities that make water bodies dirty and the impact of polluted water on life.
key_ideas: Washing clothes or bathing animals in rivers causes pollution
Factory waste makes water harmful
Polluted water harms fish and plants

concepts.title: Living and Non-Living Things
concepts.description: Living and Non-Living Things — part of the chapter on Our Environment.
key_ideas: Core principles of living and non-living things
Step-by-step problem solving for living and non-living things
Real-world applications of living and non-living things

concepts.title: Effects of Deforestation
concepts.description: Effects of Deforestation — part of the chapter on Our Environment.
key_ideas: Core principles of effects of deforestation
Step-by-step problem solving for effects of deforestation
Real-world applications of effects of deforestation

concepts.title: Interdependence in Nature
concepts.description: Explains how living things depend on non-living things (like air, water, and soil) and on other living things for survival.
key_ideas: Plants need sunlight, water, and soil to grow
Animals depend on plants for food and oxygen
The relationship between biotic and abiotic components

concepts.title: Types of Pollution
concepts.description: Identifies the different ways the environment gets dirty or harmful, focusing on air, water, land, and noise pollution.
key_ideas: Causes of air pollution (smoke from vehicles and factories)
Causes of water pollution (dumping waste in rivers)
Impact of noise pollution on health

concepts.title: Biodegradable vs Non-biodegradable Waste
concepts.description: Differentiates between waste materials that rot and mix with the soil and those that remain in the environment for a long time.
key_ideas: Biodegradable items (fruit peels, paper)
Non-biodegradable items (plastic, glass)
Why plastic is harmful to the soil and animals

concepts.title: The 3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
concepts.description: Teaches actionable methods to minimize waste and protect the environment through the three R principle.
key_ideas: Reducing usage of single-use items
Reusing old jars, bags, and clothes
Recycling paper and plastic to make new products

concepts.title: Conservation of Natural Resources
concepts.description: Discusses the importance of saving natural resources like water, forests, and fuel for future generations.
key_ideas: Methods to save water at home
Importance of planting more trees (Afforestation)
Using electricity wisely

concepts.title: Organ Systems — Digestive, Respiratory
concepts.description: Organ Systems — Digestive, Respiratory — part of the chapter on Our Body.
key_ideas: Core principles of organ systems
Step-by-step problem solving for organ systems
Real-world applications of organ systems

concepts.title: Common Diseases and Prevention
concepts.description: Common Diseases and Prevention — part of the chapter on Our Body.
key_ideas: Core principles of common diseases and prevention
Step-by-step problem solving for common diseases and prevention
Real-world applications of common diseases and prevention

concepts.title: Sense Organs and Their Care
concepts.description: Introduction to the five sense organs, their specific functions in helping us perceive the world, and how to keep them clean and healthy.
key_ideas: The five sense organs: Eyes, Ears, Nose, Tongue, Skin
Functions: Seeing, Hearing, Smelling, Tasting, Touching
Hygiene and protection of sense organs

concepts.title: Teeth: Types, Structure, and Care
concepts.description: Understanding the difference between temporary and permanent teeth, the four types of teeth based on function, and the basics of oral hygiene to prevent cavities.
key_ideas: Milk teeth vs. Permanent teeth
Types of teeth: Incisors, Canines, Premolars, Molars
Tooth decay and proper brushing techniques
Introduction to microbes (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa)

concepts.title: The Framework: Bones and Muscles
concepts.description: Exploration of the skeletal system that gives shape to the body and the muscular system that enables movement.
key_ideas: The Skeleton: Skull, Ribcage, Backbone, and Limbs
Joints: Where two bones meet to allow movement
How muscles contract and relax to move bones
Importance of calcium and protein

concepts.title: Circulatory and Excretory Systems
concepts.description: A basic overview of how blood transports materials through the body and how the body removes waste products.
key_ideas: The Heart: Pumping blood to all body parts
Blood vessels: Arteries and Veins
The Kidneys: Filtering waste to form urine
The Skin: Removing waste through sweat

concepts.title: Posture, Exercise, and Rest
concepts.description: Learning the importance of correct body posture while sitting or standing, the role of regular exercise, and the necessity of adequate sleep.
key_ideas: Correct posture for a healthy backbone
Benefits of exercise for muscle strength
Why the body needs sleep and rest
Recreation and mental health

concepts.title: Directions — North, South, East, West
concepts.description: Directions — North, South, East, West — part of the chapter on Maps and Globe.
key_ideas: Core principles of directions
Step-by-step problem solving for directions
Real-world applications of directions

concepts.title: Reading Simple Maps
concepts.description: Reading Simple Maps — part of the chapter on Maps and Globe.
key_ideas: Core principles of reading simple maps
Step-by-step problem solving for reading simple maps
Real-world applications of reading simple maps

concepts.title: The Globe: A Model of the Earth
concepts.description: Understanding that a globe is a miniature, spherical model representing the Earth, showing how the Earth looks from space.
key_ideas: A globe is round like a ball
It rotates on an axis just like the Earth
It shows the correct shape of continents and oceans

concepts.title: Using Landmarks
concepts.description: Identifying important buildings, trees, or natural features that help us remember a path or find a location.
key_ideas: Landmarks are reference points used for navigation
They help describe where a place is located
Examples include schools, hospitals, parks, or statues

concepts.title: Map Symbols and Keys
concepts.description: Learning to interpret the small pictures (symbols) and colors used on maps to represent real-world objects, using a legend or key.
key_ideas: Maps use symbols because real objects are too big to draw
A 'Key' or 'Legend' explains what each symbol means
Standard colors represent features (e.g., blue for water, green for forests)

concepts.title: Continents and Oceans
concepts.description: Identifying and naming the large landmasses (continents) and vast water bodies (oceans) located on a globe or world map.
key_ideas: The Earth is made up of land and water
Large land masses are called Continents
Large water bodies are called Oceans
Water covers more of the Earth than land

concepts.title: Difference Between Maps and Globes
concepts.description: Comparing the advantages and limitations of using a flat map versus a spherical globe.
key_ideas: A map is a flat drawing; a globe is a round model
Maps are easy to carry; globes are bulky
Maps can show small details (like a city); globes show the whole world
